arguments.data: rdi; pointer to the input bytes. Read on every arm except length 0, never written on any arm
arguments.length: rsi; the input length in bytes; selects the arm by the dispatch bounds 3/8/16/32/64/96/128/240
arguments.seed: rdx; a 64-bit seed folded into every lane constant as (K + seed) on a pair's first lane and (K - seed) on its second lane

final_mix: final_mix(x): y = x ^ (x >> 37); y = y * 0x165667b19e3779f9 (mod 2^64); result = y ^ (y >> 32). Shared by every in-window arm; the 9..16 arm reaches it inline at 0x61c3581, the small arms tail-jump into its second half at 0x61c358b, the accumulator arms compute it inline at 0x61c371a

mix_primitive: a lane pair reads two consecutive qwords; x = (K1 + seed) ^ first, y = (K2 - seed) ^ second; the pair contributes fold(x, y) = (x*y mod 2^64) ^ (x*y >> 64) (the low and high halves of the 128-bit product, xored)
return_value: rax: the 64-bit hash of the input under the seed (lengths 0..128); for lengths 129 and above, whatever the delegation target returns for the same (data, length, seed)
side_effects: none: no stores, no calls, no reads outside the input's own bytes (overlapping lane reads stay inside [data, data+length) on every arm), callee-saved registers rbx/rbp/r12-r15 untouched (r12/r14/r15 are pushed and popped on the accumulator arms only)
